title: Otto the Great
fact_summary: The king whose army defeated the Hungarians in 955. The sources on this map disagree on whether to call him king or emperor for that year.

claims.text: Liudprand calls him “sanctissimi atque invictissimi regis Ottonis”, the most holy and unconquered king Otto, whose power now terrifies the Hungarians.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: The Metz annal for 955 says the Hungarians were defeated “ab Ottone imperatore”, by the Emperor Otto.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: Widukind, describing the 955 campaign, calls him the king and places him in the fifth, “Royal”, legion.
claims.certainty_reason: Read in English translation in the open copy linked under Sources.

contradictions.what_differs: His title in 955: the Metz annal calls him emperor, Widukind calls him king. This may only show when each was written, not a disagreement about events.

open_questions.text: When was Otto crowned emperor, and was the Metz entry written after that?

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.
